I farm the way I know best: steady, practical, and not too risky. I have 12 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, with well irrigation, so I will keep the full area in the usual double-cropping system because that fits my land, my experience, and my household labor. At my age, I will not do anything complicated or experimental. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate a few key times, and use rotary tillage because it is easier to manage and suits my routine. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stable yield, give it enough nitrogen, irrigate when needed through the well, and continue with rotary tillage after wheat. I will control pests only as much as needed, not excessively, because I want to protect yield but also avoid wasting money. My goal this year is stable production from both crops, with manageable labor and dependable returns.
